# Sitepass — Agent Contract

Status: DRAFT (MVP v0.1.0) — syncing with implementation

English only. Machine logic must key on `code`, never on `message`.

---

## Overview

Sitepass publishes a static site build on a temporary public URL. An agent
builds the project locally, packs the output, and uploads it via HTTP.
Anonymous use needs no account. Optional username+password accounts (no
email verification) get a longer token TTL and a list of their previews.
The human creates a token in the browser and hands it to the agent.

Base API path: `/api/v1` on the **control host** only
(e.g. `https://sitepass.tech`). Preview hosts (`https://<label>.sitepass.tech`)
serve static files only — never POST `/api/v1/upload` there.

All API responses: `application/json; charset=utf-8` (except this file)

Success envelope: `{ "ok": true, ...payload }`
Failure envelope: `{ "ok": false, "error": { "code", "message", "details", "token_consumed", "docs" } }`

On upload errors, `token_consumed` is always present. Rejections never consume the token.

Agent environments need outbound HTTPS to the control host. Localhost will not work.

### DNS failures (required retry before asking the human)

If name resolution fails (`Temporary failure in name resolution`, `getaddrinfo failed`,
`Name or service not known`):

1. Do **not** immediately hand off to the human.
2. Resolve the control hostname with DNS-over-HTTPS, e.g.
   `https://cloudflare-dns.com/dns-query?name=CONTROL_HOST&type=A` (Accept: application/dns-json)
   or `https://dns.google/resolve?name=CONTROL_HOST&type=A`.
3. Retry the upload connecting to that IPv4 while keeping TLS SNI / Host as CONTROL_HOST:
   `curl --resolve CONTROL_HOST:443:IP https://CONTROL_HOST/api/v1/upload ...`
4. Only if DoH and IP connect also fail, ask the human to run the curl locally.

Never POST `/api/v1/upload` to a preview subdomain.

---

## Endpoints

### POST /api/v1/tokens

Public. Rate limited per IP. If a session cookie is present, the token is
owned by that user and uses the `registered` plan (longer TTL).

Create an upload token. Optional body: `{ "project_name": "landing" }` (max 48 chars).

Returns 201: token (shown once), token_id, preview_url, expires_at,
expires_in_seconds, limits.

### POST /api/v1/auth/register

Public. No email. Body: `{ "username", "password" }`.
Username: 3–32 chars `[A-Za-z0-9_]`. Password: min 8 chars.
Sets HttpOnly session cookie. Returns 201 `{ user: { id, username } }`.

### POST /api/v1/auth/login

Public. Body: `{ "username", "password" }`. Sets session cookie.
Returns 200 `{ user: { id, username } }`.

### POST /api/v1/auth/logout

Clears session. Returns 204.

### GET /api/v1/auth/me

Session required. Returns `{ user: { id, username } }`.

### GET /api/v1/me/tokens

Session required. Returns `{ tokens: [ { token_id, project_name, preview_url,
subdomain, expires_at, expires_in_seconds, revision, has_build, live } ] }`.

### POST /api/v1/upload

**Control host only.** Do not call this on a preview subdomain.

Header: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`

Body: `multipart/form-data` with part named `archive`, or `application/octet-stream`
(raw archive bytes). Prefer octet-stream for agent uploads.

Optional header: `X-Content-SHA256` (hex digest of body).

Returns 200: preview_url, revision, expires_at, expires_in_seconds,
file_count, size_bytes, warnings[].

Concurrent uploads on one token return 409 `upload_in_progress`.

### GET /api/v1/status

Header: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`

Returns token state: preview_url, expires_at, expires_in_seconds, revision,
has_build, upload_count.

### DELETE /api/v1/token

Header: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`

Revokes the token and removes content immediately. Returns 204.

### GET /api/v1/health

Public, unauthenticated.

Returns: status (`healthy` | `degraded` | `read_only`), accepting_uploads,
disk_usage_percent.

`read_only` when `SITEPASS_READ_ONLY` is set — uploads and new tokens rejected.
`degraded` when disk is at/above high-water (or usage cannot be measured).
`accepting_uploads` is false only in `read_only`. At high-water, existing
tokens may still upload; only new token creation is refused.

### Capacity behaviour

- High-water: `POST /tokens` → `storage_capacity_exceeded`. Uploads continue.
- Critical: reaper revokes oldest live tokens (by created_at) until usage
  falls below high-water; content removed; tokens marked revoked.
- Per-IP token creation and per-token upload hourly limits → `rate_limited`.
- Maintenance: `SITEPASS_READ_ONLY=true` → `service_read_only` on tokens/upload.
- Concurrent unpack cap / low memory → `service_overloaded` (Retry-After).
- Critical disk also pauses uploads until the reaper frees space.

### GET /llms.txt

Plain text agent contract (this file). Cache-Control: public, max-age=300.

---

## Artifact contract

### Accepted formats (detected from content, not filename)

- `.tar.gz` — gzip magic, then tar
- `.zip` — PK magic
- `.tar.zst` — zstd magic, then tar
- single `.html` — HTML content type or `<` as first non-space byte (published as index.html)

### Limits (defaults; read from plan at runtime)

| Limit | Default |
|---|---|
| Compressed size | 100 MB |
| Uncompressed size | 300 MB |
| File count | 5000 |
| Compression ratio | 200:1 |
| Path depth | 32 |
| Path segment length | 255 bytes |
| Total path length | 4096 bytes |

### Entry validation (fail-closed)

Reject the entire upload if any entry:

- Escapes the destination root after cleaning
- Is absolute or contains `..`
- Contains a null byte or backslash
- Is not a regular file or directory (no symlinks, hardlinks, devices, FIFOs, sockets)
- Exceeds running uncompressed total or file count limits

Partial content is never published. Staging directory is removed on rejection.

### Entry point resolution

1. If `index.html` exists at archive root, that root is the site.
2. Else if archive root contains exactly one directory and no files, descend one level and repeat.
3. Else reject with `entrypoint_not_found`.

Descent is limited to one level.

### Warnings (non-blocking)

- `missing_assets` — index.html references files absent from archive (up to 10 paths)
- `large_bundle` — a single file exceeds 2 MB
- `source_tree_present` — node_modules/, src/, or .git/ present in published tree

---

## Error codes

All upload rejection codes have `token_consumed: false`.

### token_not_found

HTTP 404. Unknown token.

### token_expired

HTTP 410. Token lifetime elapsed.

### token_revoked

HTTP 410. Token deleted by its holder.

### upload_in_progress

HTTP 409. Another upload is being processed for this token.

### archive_too_large

HTTP 413. Compressed size over limit.

### archive_unpacked_too_large

HTTP 413. Uncompressed size over limit.

### archive_too_many_files

HTTP 413. File count over limit.

### archive_malformed

HTTP 422. Not readable as the detected format.

### archive_unsafe_entry

HTTP 422. Path traversal, symlink, or non-regular entry.

### unsupported_format

HTTP 415. Not tar.gz, zip, tar.zst, or html.

### entrypoint_not_found

HTTP 422. No index.html at the root or one level down.

### checksum_mismatch

HTTP 422. X-Content-SHA256 does not match the body.

### project_name_invalid

HTTP 422. Name is too long or produces an empty slug.

### rate_limited

HTTP 429. Per-IP or per-token limit. Response includes Retry-After.

### storage_capacity_exceeded

HTTP 503. Disk above the high-water mark.

### service_read_only

HTTP 503. Maintenance mode.

### service_overloaded

HTTP 503. Host is temporarily out of upload capacity (too many concurrent
unpacks, or free memory below the configured floor). Response includes
Retry-After. Retry later; the token is not consumed.

### internal_error

HTTP 500. Unexpected failure. Response includes a correlation id.

### auth_invalid

HTTP 401. Wrong username or password.

### auth_conflict

HTTP 409. Username already taken.

### auth_unauthorized

HTTP 401. Session missing or expired.

### wrong_host

HTTP 404 from a preview subdomain if `/api/*` is requested there.
Upload and other API calls belong on the control host only.

---

## Worked examples

### Example 1 — create a token and upload a tar.gz

```bash
# 1. Human creates a token (or copies the instruction from the control UI).
curl -sS -X POST https://CONTROL/api/v1/tokens \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"project_name":"landing"}'

# Response includes token (shown once), preview_url, expires_at.

# 2. Agent packs the production build and uploads it to CONTROL — not to preview_url.
curl -sS -X POST https://CONTROL/api/v1/upload \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/octet-stream' \
  --data-binary @dist.tar.gz

# 3. Open preview_url in a browser. Re-upload with the same token to replace the site.
```

### Example 2 — check status, then revoke

```bash
curl -sS https://CONTROL/api/v1/status \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN"

curl -sS -X DELETE https://CONTROL/api/v1/token \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN"
# 204 — preview content is removed immediately
```
